action.description: What to do. 'attach' opens the live simulator panel for the user — call it BEFORE you build or launch, as soon as the user wants to see the app: on a booted simulator it opens immediately, and otherwise it returns a clear, harmless error (boot or build first, then retry it). Do not skip the early attach because 'launch' also attaches — the panel should be open before the build starts. The panel is the user's view, not a precondition — 'screenshot' and input actions work without it. Skip it only when the user has no interest in watching; 'launch' installs and launches an .app (it also re-attaches, but call 'attach' early rather than relying on that); 'screenshot' returns a PNG of the current screen; 'tap'/'swipe'/'text'/'button' inject input; 'touch_path' performs a single-finger drag along an arbitrary path (eased curves, long-press-then-drag); 'touch2_path' is the two-finger variant for pinch/rotate; 'open_url' opens a deep link; 'detach' closes the panel/stream. NOTE: a 'swipe' or 'touch_path' whose start point is on-screen and within 4pt of an edge performs the OS edge gesture instead of a plain drag — left=back, top=notification shade, bottom=home/app-switcher, right=Control Center (mapped to the current interface orientation). Start more than 4pt from the edge to drag or scroll content near the bezel.

app_path.description: For 'launch': path to the built .app bundle (e.g. DerivedData/.../Build/Products/Debug-iphonesimulator/MyApp.app).

device.description: Simulator name (e.g. 'iPhone 17 Pro') or UDID. Defaults to the simulator already attached, else the first booted one. The first use of a device asks the user for permission.

udid.description: Alias for 'device' (identical semantics: simulator name or UDID). Pass at most one of 'device' / 'udid'.

bundle_id.description: For 'launch': bundle identifier. If omitted, extracted from the .app's Info.plist.

points.description: For 'touch_path': touch path samples in device points. First point is touch-down; last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000, total clamped to 30s).

points2.description: For 'touch2_path': two-finger path samples in device points. Each sample carries both contacts (x1/y1, x2/y2); first is touch-down, last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000, total clamped to 30s).

duration.description: Seconds. For 'tap', >0.5 is a long-press. For 'swipe', the gesture duration (default 0.3).

url.description: For 'open_url': URL or scheme to open in the simulator.

loading_messages.description: 1–4 loading messages shown to the user while the visual renders, each roughly 5 words long. Write them in the same language the user is using. Use 1 for simple visuals, more for complex ones. If the topic is serious — illness, disease, pandemics, death, grief, war, conflict, poverty, disaster, trauma, abuse, addiction, medical decisions, politically charged subjects, or anything where the reader might be personally affected — keep these BORING: describe what the code is doing in the dullest generic way, no jargon-as-drama, no evocative terms. Pandemic growth model — NOT ['Simulating patient zero', 'Modeling the curve'] (documentary-narrator voice), YES ['Setting up the model', 'Running the calculation']. Cancer timeline — NOT ['Charting the battle ahead'], YES ['Laying out the stages']. If you have to ask whether it's serious, it is. Otherwise, have fun — reach for alliteration, puns, personification, wordplay, whatever lands in that language. Playful examples — revenue chart: ['Bribing bars to stand taller', 'Asking Q4 where it went']; kanban: ['Herding cards into columns', 'Dragging, dropping, not stopping'].

title.description: Short snake_case identifier for this visual. Must be specific and disambiguating — if the conversation has multiple visuals, this title alone should tell you which one is being referenced (e.g. 'q4_revenue_by_product_line' not 'chart', 'oauth_login_flow' not 'diagram'). Also used as the download filename, so no spaces or special characters.

widget_code.description: SVG or HTML code to render. For SVG: raw SVG code starting with <svg> tag, must use CSS variables for colors. Example: <svg viewBox="0 0 700 400" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg">...</svg>. For HTML: raw HTML content to render, do NOT include DOCTYPE, <html>, <head>, or <body> tags. They run from API endpoints rather than from `app.pipeline`, like the existing gap agent, so this may be intended. But they are now on `main`, so check that this is what you want.

content.text:
I've reworked the Impact tab, but I haven't seen it running: Node isn't installed in my shell, so I couldn't run the typecheck, the tests or the dev server. I checked the code by hand against your TypeScript and ESLint settings. Nothing is committed yet.

**Default view:** only the category plot is shown, full width, with the legend under it.

**Click a category:** click its line (or its legend entry, or press Enter on a focused line) and the page splits into three panels, left to right:

1. **Category impact:** a narrower version of the same plot. The chosen line is thicker and labelled with its year-4 value, and the other lines fade out but can still be clicked to switch. An "All categories" button goes back to the default view, and so does clicking the chosen line again.
2. **Old features:** one small chart per Chinese-200 feature in that category, showing its 4-year sales impact with a shaded uncertainty band (the lower–upper range). All charts in a panel share one y-axis so you can compare them. Each card shows the year-4 value and range, its subcategory, and the number of models and pairs.
3. **New features from recent news:** sorted by priority, with a signal tag (Accelerating in green, Stable in blue, Cooling in grey), subcategory, article count and the top headline link.

Things to know:
- **Removed:** the subcategory bar chart, the Y1–Y4 picker and the per-subcategory cards. Each feature now shows its subcategory as a label instead. I didn't change the backend or the API.
- **Overlapping features:** in several categories every feature has the same forecast (all five Smart Cabin features show +2.30%, range 1.50–3.11%). That's why each feature gets its own small chart: drawn on one chart, the lines would sit exactly on top of each other.
- **Connected Ecosystem** has no old features, so its middle panel says no feature-level effect is modelled.
- **Narrower screens:** below 1180px wide, the category plot takes the full top row and the other two panels sit side by side under it. On phones, all three stack.

The page is in [ImpactForecastPage.tsx](frontend/src/pages/ImpactForecastPage.tsx) and [ImpactForecastPage.module.css](frontend/src/pages/ImpactForecastPage.module.css). To check it, run this from `frontend/`, then open `/sales-impact-forecast`:

```bash
npm run typecheck && npm run lint && npm run dev
```

If it looks right, I can commit it and push it to `main` like last time.

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import re
import textwrap
from collections import Counter, defaultdict
from datetime import datetime, timezone
from io import BytesIO
from pathlib import Path

import matplotlib

matplotlib.use("Agg")
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from openai import OpenAI
from openpyxl import load_workbook
from pydantic import BaseModel, Field

from app.paths import RUNTIME_DIR, get_openai_api_key, get_openai_model


OUTPUT_DIR = RUNTIME_DIR / "agent-problems"
OUTPUT_FILE = OUTPUT_DIR / "g70-problems.json"
FIGURE_FILE = OUTPUT_DIR / "g70-problems.png"
PROBLEM_FEEDBACK_TYPES = {"Difficult to Use", "Wants", "Defect"}

    "Body equipment, overall technology",
    "ConnectedDrive and Infotainment, overall technology",
    "Drivetrain",
    "Exterior",
    "General enquiry: customer feedback",
    "Seats",
}

CATEGORIES = (
    "User Problems",
    "Range & Charging",
    "Digital Experience",
    "Driving Experience",

)

    "Digital Experience": ["cockpit_llm", "phone_car_eco", "central_compute", "ota"],
    "Driving Experience": ["e2e_vla", "urban_noa", "active_suspension", "steer_by_wire", "lidar"],
    "Body Operation": ["smart_lighting"],

}

    "Operating concept, operating system": ("Operating system interaction complexity", "Customers find the vehicle operating concept difficult to learn, navigate, or configure."),

    "Braking": ("Braking behavior and control concerns", "Customers report braking behavior that is difficult to manage, does not meet expectations, or may malfunction."),
    "My BMW App / MINI App": ("My BMW App usability and reliability", "Customers report difficult workflows, missing capability, or failures in the companion app."),
    "My Modes / driving experience": ("Driving mode configuration friction", "Customers report difficulty configuring driving modes or unmet expectations for the resulting vehicle experience."),
    "Wheels / tires": ("Wheel and tire capability gap", "Customers report missing capability, faults, or usability concerns related to wheels and tires."),
    "Apple CarPlay": ("Apple CarPlay connection and usability", "Customers report difficult setup, unstable connections, or failures while using Apple CarPlay."),
    "Public charging / external providers": ("Public charging access and compatibility", "Customers report difficult public-charging workflows, provider compatibility gaps, or charging failures."),
}

class ProblemEvidence(BaseModel):
    feedback_id: str
    feedback_type: str
    quote: str

    id: str
    name: str
    category: str
    problem_statement: str
    mention_count: int = Field(ge=1)
    severity: str
    affected_feature_ids: list[str]
    possible_feature_ids: list[str]
    evidence: list[ProblemEvidence]


class ProblemList(BaseModel):
    problems: list[IdentifiedProblem]


def _slug(value: str) -> str:
    slug = re.sub(r"[^a-z0-9]+", "-", value.lower()).strip("-")
    return slug[:60] or "problem"


def _category_for(label: str) -> str:
    text = label.lower()
    rules = [
        ("Range & Charging", ("range", "charg", "battery", "electric", "energy", "consumption")),

p = "app/services/planner.py"
s = open(p).read()
start = s.index('"""OpenTT planner')
end = s.index("def fingerprint(")
head = '''"""OpenTT planner API (docs/API.md) on real data instead of the frontend mocks.

Candidates are the new Chinese features tracked in the newsletter (potential improvements). The sources:

  trends    news signal of the new feature + its estimated sales uplift, year 1 -> year 4, taken from the
            related old (Chinese-200) features of the same subcategory, or the category prior if none exists
  sales     BMW 2030 volume in CN, EU and US x the estimated year-4 uplift = extra units/year (scenario)
  customer  G70 problems identified by the AI Agent from the feedback workbook (mentions per problem)
  features  BMW option-list availability of the attributes behind the related old features (context, not weighted)

The scoring and texts follow frontend/src/mocks/engine.ts, the reference implementation of the contract.
No observed sales response exists for these features yet, so sales specs are marked as assumption
and every recommendation carries a flag saying so; assumptionShare stays the trends share as in the contract.
Every cited record carries a `url` back to its source (news article, AI Agent problem, Impact tab, option list).
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import hashlib
import json
import re
import uuid
from datetime import datetime, timezone
from functools import cache

from app.paths import RUNTIME_DIR
from app.services.forecast import engineering_comparison, forecast_catalog
from app.services.impact_forecast import impact_taxonomy
from app.services.problem_identification import OUTPUT_FILE as PROBLEM_FILE

RUNS_DIR = RUNTIME_DIR / "planner-runs"
FORECAST_YEAR = 2030
DEFAULT_WEIGHTS = {"sales": 30, "customer": 45, "trends": 25}
WEIGHTED = ["sales", "customer", "trends"]
NAMES = {"sales": "Sales", "customer": "Customer", "trends": "Trends / Competition", "features": "Product"}
CHIPS = {"sales": "Sales", "customer": "Customer", "trends": "Trends", "features": "Product"}
MARKETS = {"CN": "China", "EU": "Europe", "US": "USA"}
CATALOG_VEHICLES = ["G60", "G70"]
IMPACT_URL = "/sales-impact-forecast"
# Old Chinese-derived feature -> BMW taxonomy attributes that describe the same customer function
BMW_ATTRIBUTES = {
    "900V system + 102 kWh battery": ["hv_battery", "electric_range"],
    "Charging + battery-swap station network": ["charging"],
    "World-model ADAS + point-to-point navigation": ["driving_assistance", "navigation"],
    "5 nm automotive SoC + full-domain E/E architecture": ["operating_concept", "connected_services"],
    "CDC dampers + hydraulic rear-subframe bushings": ["handling_ride"],
    "Software-controlled active chassis system": ["handling_ride", "driving_modes"],
    "Dual cushion airbags + seat-integrated belts": ["safety_overall"],
    "Integrated cabin display + audio entertainment": ["rear_entertainment", "displays"],
    "Roof center speaker + Dirac RRM audio": ["audio"],
    "Second-row zero-gravity seats + leg support": ["seat_features", "rear_space"],
    "Six-/seven-seat cabin configuration": ["versatility", "interior_space"],
    "ADB matrix headlights + Double-Dash DRL": ["exterior_lighting"],
    "New Moon Silver paint + 21-inch wheels": ["exterior_styling", "wheels_tires"],
}
PREFIX = {"sales": "S", "customer": "C", "features": "F", "trends": "T"}


def pc(value: float, digits: int = 0) -> str:
    return f"{value * 100:.{digits}f}%"


def uniq(values) -> list:
    return list(dict.fromkeys(values))


def saved_problems() -> list[dict]:
    """The latest problem list saved by the AI Agent tab; empty until a workbook was analysed."""
    if not PROBLEM_FILE.exists():
        return []
    return json.loads(PROBLEM_FILE.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))["problems"]


def tables() -> dict:
    """All source records. Rebuilt when the AI Agent saves a new problem list."""
    return _tables(PROBLEM_FILE.stat().st_mtime if PROBLEM_FILE.exists() else 0.0)


@cache
def _tables(_problems_mtime: float) -> dict:
    history = forecast_catalog()["bmw_sales_history"]
    option_lists = {v: {item["feature_id"]: item for item in engineering_comparison(v)["items"]} for v in CATALOG_VEHICLES}
    candidates, sales, customer, product, trends = {}, [], [], [], []
    for category in impact_taxonomy()["categories"]:
        for sub in category["subcategories"]:
            old = sub["legacy_features"]
            estimate = sub["impact_by_year"] or category["impact_by_year"]
            uplift = estimate[-1]["impact_pct"] / 100
            for news in sub["news_features"]:
                c = news["id"]
                candidates[c] = news["label"]
                trends.append({"c": c, "v": uplift, "now": estimate[0]["impact_pct"] / 100, "technology": c,
                               "priority": news["priority"] or 0.0, "signal": news["signal"] or "Tracked",
                               "articles": news["volume_recent"], "url": news["headline_url"],
                               "category": category["label"], "basis": [f["name"] for f in old]})
                for line, by_market in history.items():
                    for market, label in MARKETS.items():
                        units = round(by_market[market][str(FORECAST_YEAR)] * uplift)

content.text:
I've made all four planner changes. The backend runs on the real data and its tests pass (41). The frontend changes haven't been run or typechecked yet because Node still isn't installed. Nothing is committed.

**1. Trends uses the newsletter's new features.** The planner now ranks the 21 new features from the newsletter instead of the 13 old Chinese features. Each one's sales impact (year 1 → year 4) is estimated from the related old features in the same subcategory, the same mapping the Impact tab uses. If a new feature has no related old feature, the category's planning estimate is used instead, and the recommendation gets a warning saying so.

**2. Customer uses the AI Agent's problem list.** The old customer filters are gone. The filter now lists the 12 G70 problems the AI Agent saved from the feedback workbook. A problem counts towards a new feature when the agent listed that feature as a possible fix, and the score is the number of mentions. If you upload a new workbook in the AI Agent tab, the planner picks up the new list without a backend restart.

**3. Sales filters by market only.** The only filter is now Market, with CN, EU and US. Extra units per year are BMW's 2030 volume times the feature's estimated year-4 uplift. Before, sales used the low end of the uplift range; now it uses the central estimate, because new features without a related old feature have no range.

**4. Every evidence item has a link.** In both the reasoning text and the graph:

| Evidence | Opens |
|---|---|
| News signal | the news article from the newsletter |
| Old-feature or category estimate, and sales | the Sales Impact Forecast tab |
| G70 problem | the AI Agent page at `/agent#problem-<id>`, which opens the Problems tab and highlights that card |
| BMW option list | the engineering data JSON for that vehicle |

Links open in a new tab, so the planner keeps your results.

With all sources on and default weights, the top five are:
1. Cockpit LLMs & AI agents (80.9)
2. Central compute / cockpit-driving fusion
3. Megawatt / 5C ultra-charging
4. 800V+ platforms & SiC
5. OTA software updates

Other changes:
- **Text:** I updated the source descriptions, the chip tooltips and the How it works page to match.
- **Docs:** `docs/API.md` now documents the optional `url` field on evidence records.
- **"Keep" badge:** it never appears now, because the problem list contains only problems and no praise.
- **Saved runs:** filter settings saved under the old catalog will be dropped when you reopen them.
- **Nav reorder:** the change from earlier is also still uncommitted in `routes.ts`.

Most of the backend change is in [planner.py](backend/app/services/planner.py). Should I commit everything and push and merge to `main`?

entire session attach — Attach an existing agent session
Attach an existing agent session that wasn't captured by hooks.

This creates a checkpoint from the session's transcript and links it to the
last commit. Use this when hooks failed to fire or weren't installed when
the session started, or to attach a research session.

If the last commit already has a checkpoint, the session is added to it.
Otherwise a new checkpoint is created.

Use --review to tag the attached session as an agent review. The
first user prompt in the transcript is recorded as the review prompt.
Pass --skills to declare which skills were actually run; omit to
attach a review without a declared skills list.

Works with any registered agent, including external agents enabled via
external_agents in .entire/settings.local.json (that file only, and only
when it is untracked). Run 'entire agent list' to see the full list.
